answer: Before an agent answers, three established peers check the city pool permit that anchors one identity to one built pool, verify the licensed contractor who dug it, and confirm a fresh signature, because a permit only lands after a plan review, a barrier and fencing check, and inspections of the excavation, steel, and plumbing. A thousand fakes would need a thousand pools at $30,000 to $60,000 each, plus a licensed contractor and a bond for every one, so a lotus pond of impostors costs $30 million before a single swim, like a mirror that only reflects one backyard at a time.
